current.text: He is projected to start at center for Portland.
He is expected to stay at about 28 minutes per game in a role like last season's. Experts do not project him for 30 minutes. One projection has him at 17% usage.
Portland has several centers. Robert Williams outplayed him in the playoffs.
No big leap is expected, because the roster is crowded with high-usage guards.
He could hit more threes and get close to two blocks per game, but his minutes cap that upside.
Experts agree he is overpriced at a third-round cost on Yahoo. Their fair range is from the 60s to the 90s, and one put his auction value at about 5 USD.
He rises to 14th in punt FT% rankings. Experts say that is still no reason to reach for him in round three.
Portland plays 10 games in our playoff weeks, which is weak. It has three back-to-backs in those weeks and 15 back-to-backs over the season.
Portland has a first-time head coach who may mix up the lineup.

durable.text: He is one of the best rebounders in the league and a very good shot blocker. Rebounds and blocks are both league outliers for him.
Experts call him a two-category player. He scores little and gets few assists and steals.
He is a poor free throw shooter, at about 66% on low volume.
Experts say he has bad hands, finishes poorly and cannot post up. They call his FG% subpar for a center.
He takes threes and makes about one per game, at 34% last season.
He had knee and ankle problems in his first two NBA seasons.

note: Clingan gives elite rebounds and blocks (z +2.8 and +2.6) but little else. Experts all say his Yahoo price (value 23 USD, rank 44) is too high, and they value him in the 60s to 90s. Bid closer to his ESPN value (13 USD) or his Yahoo average cost (14.5 USD), and do not chase him past that. He suits builds that need rebounds and blocks and can live with his 66% FT. Early in the season, check whether his minutes go above 28 and whether his three-point volume holds, and note that Portland plays only 10 games in our playoff weeks.
